items.title: Kenya exploring AI application to improve healthcare delivery
items.description: Kenya exploring AI application to improve healthcare delivery Kenya News Agency
content: The Ministry of Health is stepping-up efforts to integrate Artificial Intelligence into healthcare delivery, while strengthening doctors’ welfare and expanding access to HIV prevention services through strategic partnerships.

Principal Secretary (PS) for Medical Services, Dr Ouma Oluga, held a series of engagements at Afya House in Nairobi with representatives of global health organisations, technology experts and the Kenya Medical Practitioners, Pharmacists and Dentists Union (KMPDU), to explore ways of improving healthcare delivery and strengthening the country’s health system.

In a meeting with Ms. Anne Stake, Global Health Team Lead, at Anthropic BPC, the Ministry explored opportunities to harness artificial intelligence (AI) to improve clinical decision-making, disease surveillance, diagnostic efficiency and overall healthcare delivery.

The discussions come as Kenya accelerates its digital health transformation through the Digital Health Agency (DHA), which is spearheading efforts to strengthen digital infrastructure and equip healthcare workers with technology-driven tools to support more informed clinical decisions.

Oluga emphasised the importance of ensuring that AI applications in healthcare align with Kenya’s national AI in Health Strategy, particularly on data sovereignty, security and responsible technology use.

The engagement also highlighted the potential of AI to strengthen health systems while ensuring that emerging technologies are deployed in ways that protect patient information and support sustainable healthcare delivery.
Stake is in Kenya to engage healthcare workers and county health teams in Machakos and Nairobi as part of efforts to understand opportunities and challenges in applying AI to healthcare.
In a separate meeting, Oluga hosted KMPDU officials led by Secretary General, Dr Davji Atellah, to discuss doctors’ welfare and strengthen cooperation between the Ministry and the union.
The PS reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to constructive dialogue and sustained engagement with medical practitioners, recognising their critical contribution to healthcare service delivery.

The discussions focused on promoting the welfare of doctors and addressing issues affecting healthcare professionals, with both sides underscoring the importance of collaboration in improving the quality of health services.

Oluga also held talks with a delegation from the Elton John AIDS Foundation (EJAF) and Tiko Africa on strengthening sustainable HIV prevention programmes through increased national ownership, predictable financing and strategic partnerships.

He called for expanded access to HIV prevention services, particularly among populations at substantial risk, while urging development partners to align their support with national health priorities and strengthen existing health systems.

The meeting also examined emerging HIV prevention technologies, including long-acting injectable Lenacapavir, with Oluga stressing the need for scientific evidence, affordability, regulatory compliance and adequate health-system preparedness before their wider adoption.
The engagement explored opportunities to strengthen HIV prevention programmes, generate evidence and introduce innovative approaches to service delivery.
The delegation was led by EJAF Chief Executive Officer Anne Aslett and Tiko Africa Co-Chief Executive Officer Serah Malaba, alongside representatives from the two organisations.

The engagements reflect the Ministry’s broader focus on combining digital innovation, improved healthcare workforce welfare and strategic partnerships to build a resilient, accessible and sustainable health system.

World Toilet Day: Sanitation must become an affordable investment for every household
items.description: The 2025–2026 Kenya Mini Demographic and Health Survey shows that 76 per cent of households have access to improved sanitation facilities.
content: Access to a safe toilet is fundamental to public health, dignity and well-being. While Kenya has made progress in expanding access to improved sanitation, disparities in household circumstances, infrastructure and affordability mean that more needs to be done to extend these gains to every community.

The 2025–2026 Kenya Mini Demographic and Health Survey shows that 76 per cent of households have access to improved sanitation facilities. However, the proportion stands at 63 per cent in rural areas, compared with 93 per cent in urban areas. The survey also indicates that 45 per cent of the population has access to at least basic sanitation services, while 7.4 per cent still practise open defecation.

These findings underscore the importance of sustaining investments in sanitation while addressing the different needs of households. Access to an improved toilet is an important step, but safely managed sanitation also requires hygienic and durable facilities supported by appropriate waste containment and management systems.

The Ministry of Health’s Costed National Sanitation and Hygiene Roadmap 2023–2030 provides an indication of the investment required. It estimates that a basic G1 sanitation unit, designed to provide a clean and flyproof toilet, costs between KES 10,000 and KES 12,000 in hardware, depending on county conditions. A more durable individual G2 toilet with safe waste containment costs between KES 25,000 and KES 30,000.

items.title: Mary Wahogo urges political leaders to preach peace ahead of 2027 elections
items.description: Ambassador Mary Wahogo has called on political leaders, the youth and women to take an active role in promoting peace and preventing violence as Kenya approaches the 2027 General Election campaign period.
content: Ambassador Mary Wahogo has called on political leaders, the youth and women to take an active role in promoting peace and preventing violence as Kenya approaches the 2027 General Election campaign period.
She warned that reckless political utterances, ethnic mobilisation and incitement could trigger violence, putting lives at risk and undermining national cohesion.
Amb. Wahogo also urged politicians to exercise restraint in their public statements and avoid language that could fuel tribal animosity, confrontations or other forms of violence.

Speaking at Hennessis Hotel along Forest Road in Nairobi, Wahogo conveyed her condolences to families who have lost loved ones through violence, condemning all forms of violence that threaten the lives and safety of innocent people.
Her remarks came as thousands of women joined the UN Women team in paying tribute to women and children who have lost their lives in violent incidents.

Amb. Wahogo, who serves as Kenya Head of the International Justice, Peace and Anti-Corruption Council under the Euracia Chamber of Commerce, said women and children were particularly vulnerable during periods of instability and often suffered the greatest consequences of political and communal conflicts.

She challenged young people to resist attempts by politicians and other influential individuals to recruit them into violent activities, urging them instead to become champions of peace, national unity and the protection of lives and property.

She said the youth had an important responsibility in safeguarding the country’s future and should use their energy and influence to encourage peaceful coexistence rather than engage in confrontations driven by political interests.
Amb. Wahogo also called on women across the country to take a leading role in peacebuilding by mobilising communities, promoting dialogue and discouraging violence at the grassroots level.

She observed that women had a special responsibility to speak out against violence because they and their children frequently bear the heaviest burden when conflicts erupt, including losing family members, livelihoods and homes.
Her appeal comes amid growing efforts by national institutions, civil society organisations and international partners to prevent election-related violence ahead of the 2027 General Election.

On November 19, UN Women, in partnership with the Embassy of Ireland and the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, announced an eight-month programme aimed at protecting women and strengthening their participation in electoral peace and security in Mombasa and Kilifi counties. The initiative is being implemented by Human Rights Agenda (HURIA).
The National Cohesion and Integration Commission has also warned that political violence, public mistrust and online incitement pose significant threats to peaceful elections in 2027.
The commission has called for responsible political leadership, stronger early-warning mechanisms and greater involvement of young people in preventing electoral violence.
Separately, women leaders under the Kenyan Women for Peace initiative have committed to strengthening women’s participation in peacebuilding, dialogue and conflict prevention ahead of the elections.

Amb. Wahogo said Kenya could only safeguard its democratic progress through collective responsibility, urging political leaders, women and young people to put the country’s stability above partisan interests.
She called for peaceful political competition, respect for human life and responsible leadership, saying no political ambition should come at the expense of innocent lives.
She urged Kenyans to learn from past experiences of violence and work together to ensure that the 2027 electioneering period does not expose families and communities to unnecessary suffering.

items.title: Wangari and Thuku leave UDA for rival parties
items.description: Wangari joined Gachagua’s DCP while Thuku chose Ndindi Nyoro’s People’s Party, giving UDA two departures with different political destinations.
content: Wangari joined Gachagua’s DCP while Thuku chose Ndindi Nyoro’s People’s Party, giving UDA two departures with different political destinations.

Two UDA figures left the party on November 20 , but they did not join the same rival: Gilgil MP Martha Wangari moved to Rigathi Gachagua’s DCP, while Chinga Ward MCA Kiruga Thuku joined Ndindi Nyoro’s People’s Party. The departures put fresh attention on UDA’s support in Central Kenya ahead of the 2027 election, though the available coverage is from TUKO alone.

Thuku, elected MCA for Chinga Ward in Nyeri County, previously chaired the UDA MCA Caucus and served on the party’s National Executive Committee. He has said he intends to contest the Othaya parliamentary seat in 2027. Nyoro welcomed him alongside Kiganjo/Mathari MCA Muthoni Kuruga, who is already in the People’s Party and is seeking the Nyeri Town seat.

Nyoro predicted UDA would be wound up within weeks, saying the exodus would grow. That is his forecast, not an established account of UDA’s future. TUKO’s report does not provide a response from UDA or evidence that the party is about to dissolve.

Wangari was received by Gachagua at his Wamunyoro residence in Nyeri. She is serving her second term as Gilgil MP. TUKO reports she was elected in 2017 on a Jubilee ticket, moved to UDA in February 2022 and retained her seat that August with 35,363 votes , against 19,764 for the Jubilee candidate. She also sits on the National Assembly’s Speaker’s Panel and had voted against Gachagua’s removal as Deputy President.

Gachagua said Wangari had a mandate from her constituents to join his party. He promised free and fair nominations and urged her to strengthen her grassroots support before primaries scheduled for March 2027 . TUKO counts Naivasha MP Jayne Kihara and Kipipiri MP Wanjiku Muhia among the UDA-elected MPs already in DCP, making Wangari the third in that group.

The reports’ central distinction is easy to miss if the departures are treated as one bloc: Wangari went to Gachagua, while Thuku went to Nyoro. The first TUKO report frames both moves as pressure on UDA in Central Kenya; its earlier report focuses on Wangari and DCP’s expanding ranks. The coverage also gives different names for Gachagua’s party: one report calls it the Democratic Change Party, while the other uses Democracy for the Citizens Party. The reports do not explain the discrepancy.

TUKO’s broader account lists other figures who have moved from UDA to DCP, including governors Irungu Kang’ata and Kiarie Badilisha, senator Tabitha Karanja, and the Nyeri County Assembly. It also says Gachagua received three legislators on November 17 and names other MPs who switched earlier in November. Those details describe a wider run of defections, but they do not establish how many members have left UDA nationally.

The reports do not quantify the effect of the departures on UDA’s membership, support or organisation in Central Kenya. Nor do they independently verify Gachagua’s claim that 60 UDA members in various roles have privately asked him to reserve places for them. That claim should be kept separate from confirmed public defections.

Gachagua has set December 31, 2026 as the deadline for defections into DCP, according to TUKO. The next concrete test will be whether more UDA members cross over before then, and whether Wangari and other DCP aspirants can secure the party nominations promised for March.

Australia Introduces New Mandatory Visa Law Banning Visitors From Visa Hopping From November 28
items.description: Australia will impose Condition 8503 on visitor visa holders from 28 November 2026, blocking switches to work, student and partner visas while in Australia.
content: PAY ATTENTION: Mark TUKO.co.ke as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed!

Elijah Ntongai is an experienced editor at TUKO.co.ke, with more than four years in financial, business, labour and technology reporting. His work provides valuable insights into Kenyan, African, and global trends
Australia will enforce a sweeping immigration restriction from November 28, 2026, barring most visitor visa holders from applying to switch to other visa categories while remaining in the country.

The changes were formalised through the Migration Amendment (Preventing Further Stay for Visitor Visas) Regulations 2026, signed by Governor-General Sam Mostyn on November 12, 2026, under the Migration Act 1958.

The regulations amend the existing Migration Regulations 1994.
PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.
The amendment makes Condition 8503, known as the "No Further Stay" condition, mandatory across three visitor visa categories:
Previously, the condition applied automatically to some Subclass 600 streams but could be applied at the immigration minister's discretion in others.
The new regulations remove that flexibility and standardise the restriction across all three visa types.
Under Condition 8503, a visitor generally cannot lodge a valid onshore application for any other substantive visa, with the exception of a protection visa, unless the minister grants a waiver.

The explanatory statement accompanying the regulations confirms this, stating that the condition "provides that the holder will not, after entering Australia, be entitled to be granted a substantive visa, other than a protection visa, while the holder remains in Australia."

This effectively closes the door on visitors attempting to transition onshore to employer-sponsored, student, partner or skilled migration pathways after arrival.
The Australian Government says the amendments are designed to ensure visitor visas serve their intended purpose: facilitating short-term stays.
The changes aim to "facilitate short-term visits and limit onshore visa hopping and pathways that facilitate extended onshore residence."

The government also expects the regulations to contribute to managing overall migration levels and reducing net overseas migration, while discouraging non-genuine applicants from using visitor visas as a gateway to successive temporary visa applications.
The new conditions apply only to applications lodged on or after November 28, 2026.
People who already hold valid visitor visas will not be retrospectively affected, nor will applicants who submit their applications before the commencement date.
The government confirmed it will retain the power to waive Condition 8503 in qualifying circumstances under the existing provisions of subregulation 2.05 of the Migration Regulations.
Waivers are not automatic and must be applied for individually.

Foreign nationals planning to visit Australia are advised to determine their intended immigration pathway before travelling.

Those considering employment, education or long-term residence in Australia should pursue the appropriate visa category from outside the country rather than assuming they can make the switch after arrival.

In other news, Australia will introduce stricter assessments of Bridging Visa B (BVB) applications linked to employer-sponsored visa pathways from November 30 , 2026, requiring foreign workers to provide stronger evidence that overseas travel is necessary.

The changes affect applicants awaiting decisions on Skills in Demand (Subclass 482), Employer Nomination Scheme (Subclass 186) and Skilled Employer Sponsored Regional (Subclass 494) visas, as well as their included family members.

Applicants will need to provide specific travel dates, itineraries and supporting documents such as medical records, business invitations or evidence of family events, with general holiday or family visit explanations potentially insufficient on their own.
The BVB application fee stands at AUD 575 (approximately KSh 48,000), while applications lodged before November 30 will continue under the existing assessment approach.

items.description: Senate Majority Leader Aaron Cheruiyot joined traders in Kisumu West, Kisumu, at the invitation of Hon. Rozzah Buyu, to recognise and boost smallholder
content: Senate Majority Leader Aaron Cheruiyot joined traders in Kisumu West, Kisumu, at the invitation of Hon. Rozzah Buyu, to recognise and boost smallholder traders.Cheruiyot described traders, in all their diverse crafts, as the most effective drivers of the economy at the grassroots.

He said traders work tirelessly and devise innovative strategies to navigate the complexities and overcome the challenges of the business world, often with little support but with great determination.
To recognise their hard work, the leaders boosted the businesses of smallholder traders in the constituency, offering encouragement and support to help them grow.

Speaking at the event, Cheruiyot said the initiative was guided by the Usawa Agenda, which seeks to uplift every Kenyan to lead a decent life and build a nation where everyone is valued and appreciated.
He said the agenda is about fairness, dignity and equal opportunity, ensuring that no Kenyan, however small their business, is left behind.

Cheruiyot thanked the people of Kisumu for their overwhelming support for the Broad-Based Government and for their decision to grant President William Samoei Ruto another mandate to strengthen national unity and implement progressive policies for all Kenyans.
He said the support shown in Kisumu was a sign of growing trust in the government’s agenda of inclusion, economic empowerment and national cohesion.

The National Police Service (NPS) has issued a formal public notice ahead of its Police Constable recruitment drive on December 10, 2026.

items.title: Equity Bank Announces 18 Job Vacancies in Kenya – November 2026
items.description: Equity Bank has announced multiple career opportunities for professionals interested in joining its operations in Kenya and supporting programmes extending…
content: Equity Bank has announced multiple career opportunities for professionals interested in joining its operations in Kenya and supporting programmes extending across different markets. The latest recruitment drive features 18 vacancies covering banking, financial crime compliance, data and analytics, project management, climate adaptation finance, monitoring and evaluation, gender and social inclusion, youth banking and the creative economy.

The opportunities provide openings for professionals at different management and specialist levels. Several positions are focused on strengthening the Bank’s regulatory compliance and financial crime management framework, including transaction monitoring, KYC advisory, AML policies, regulatory change and data-driven compliance testing.

Other vacancies support the Africa Rural Climate Adaptation Finance Mechanism (ARCAFIM), including positions concerned with programme coordination, climate adaptation banking, gender and social inclusion, and monitoring and evaluation. Equity Bank is also recruiting professionals to support its Youth Banking and Creative Economy portfolios.

Equity Bank Kenya Limited describes itself as a technology-driven financial services institution whose operations include banking, insurance, payments, technology, investment and social impact. Its broader strategy focuses on financial inclusion, economic empowerment, innovation and sustainable development.

Applicants should carefully review the requirements attached to their preferred position before submitting an application. Closing dates vary, with some of the earliest vacancies closing on November 24, 2026.
Below are the 18 Equity Bank job vacancies currently advertised.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: December 17, 2026

Equity Bank is recruiting a Regional Coordinator for its operations in Kenya. The position provides an opportunity for a professional interested in supporting regional-level coordination and implementation.

As a coordination position, the successful candidate will operate within the structures established by the Bank for the relevant programme or business area and support effective delivery across the assigned region.

Candidates interested in this position should refer to the official Equity Bank vacancy notice for the complete job description, responsibilities and eligibility requirements before applying. This is particularly important because the vacancy information supplied for this listing does not contain the full detailed job description.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 27, 2026

The Senior AML Manager – Transaction Monitoring will strengthen the effectiveness of Equity Bank’s risk-based Anti-Money Laundering, Counter Financing of Terrorism and Counter Proliferation Financing transaction-monitoring framework.

The position provides Second Line governance over transaction-monitoring coverage, scenario development and calibration, alert quality and data integrity. It also supports escalation of suspicious activity to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer.
The role also maintains the Bank’s documented transaction-monitoring framework and supports regulatory inspections, independent reviews and audits.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 27, 2026
The Manager – Transaction Monitoring will support the assessment and strengthening of Equity Bank’s risk-based AML/CFT/CPF transaction-monitoring controls.
The position focuses on monitoring coverage, detection scenarios, alert-management standards, data completeness and escalation of potentially suspicious activity.
The position also supports regulatory inspections, independent reviews and audits involving transaction-monitoring controls.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 27, 2026
The Manager – Testing (Data & Analytics) will plan and execute independent, data-driven Second Line testing of financial crime and regulatory controls.
The role uses analytics and data testing to assess controls, identify exceptions and document evidence-based findings and their root causes.
The role is particularly focused on producing testing that is documented, repeatable and capable of independent review.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 26, 2026

The Senior Manager – Testing (Data & Analytics) will independently evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of regulatory and financial crime controls using data-driven Second Line testing methodologies.
The position leads population-based testing, analytics and continuous monitoring while providing management and Board committees with information about control effectiveness.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 26, 2026

This position is responsible for proactive identification, interpretation, governance and oversight of regulatory changes, compliance policies, standards and regulatory obligations affecting the Bank.
The Senior Compliance Manager will help translate regulatory requirements into clear policies, accountable ownership and effective controls.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 26, 2026
The Senior Manager – KYC Advisory will provide specialist risk-based advice concerning Know Your Customer, Customer Due Diligence and Enhanced Due Diligence requirements.
The position provides independent challenge and oversight of financial-crime risks associated with customers and complex relationships.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 26, 2026
The Manager – Regulatory Change, AML Policies & Standards will support the identification and interpretation of AML/CFT/CPF regulatory developments.
The role is also responsible for maintaining relevant policies, standards and the Bank’s regulatory-obligations register.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 26, 2026
The Manager – Project Management Office will coordinate governance, planning, monitoring and reporting for complex regulatory-remediation and compliance-transformation programmes.
The position is intended to ensure that commitments made to regulators are properly tracked and delivered while risks and delays are escalated through appropriate governance structures.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 26, 2026
The Manager – AML & KYC Advisory will provide risk-based AML/CFT/CPF and KYC advisory opinions concerning customer onboarding, retention and higher-risk customer relationships.
The role provides independent review and challenge while ensuring that advisory decisions are appropriately documented.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 26, 2026
The Gender & Social Inclusion Coordinator will lead the technical-assistance and inclusion agenda under ARCAFIM.

The role focuses on enabling small-scale rural producers and small and medium-sized agribusinesses to access and sustainably benefit from climate-responsive financing, with particular attention to women, youth, low-income rural producers and underserved communities.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 26, 2026

The Climate Change Adaptation Banking Coordinator will lead the design, rollout and performance management of ARCAFIM’s climate-change-adaptation lending component across participating Equity Bank Group subsidiaries.
The position will help expand climate-resilient financing for small-scale rural producers and value-chain actors, including women and young people.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 26, 2026
The Monitoring & Evaluation Officer will lead the design and operation of ARCAFIM’s monitoring, evaluation and learning framework.
The position will provide evidence concerning programme lending, technical assistance and outcomes while supporting reporting to Equity Bank management and IFAD.
The official vacancy also identifies results-based management, survey design, data analysis, digital M&E tools and data-quality assurance as important areas for the position.
Location: Multiple Locations Closing Date: November 26, 2026
The Programme Coordinator will lead planning, coordination and delivery of ARCAFIM across participating Equity Bank entities.
The role provides strategic and operational oversight of the Programme Management Unit while coordinating climate-change-adaptation financing and capacity-building activities.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 24, 2026

The Relationship Manager – Youth Banking will lead growth and development of Equity Bank’s youth portfolio by expanding customer acquisition, strengthening banking relationships and encouraging digital adoption.
The role will also develop partnerships across youth-focused ecosystems and support growth in deposits, responsible lending and revenue.
Location: Multiple Locations Closing Date: November 24, 2026
Equity Bank is seeking a Data & Innovation Manager to support its Youth Banking business.
The position sits within an area of the Bank that uses technology, data and innovation to expand financial inclusion and develop financial solutions for younger customers.

The successful candidate will work within the Bank’s Youth Banking framework and contribute to the use of data and innovation in supporting customer growth, engagement and the continued development of youth-focused financial services.

Applicants should review the complete official Equity Bank vacancy notice for the detailed duties, experience requirements, academic requirements and other conditions attached to this particular position, as the vacancy information supplied for this article does not contain the complete job description.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 24, 2026
The Business Development Manager – Youth Banking will lead development and management of strategic partnerships that increase Equity Bank’s reach within the youth market.
The position will build youth-focused ecosystems across educational institutions, employers, technology hubs, creative industries and other strategic partners.
Location: Kenya Closing Date: November 24, 2026

The Business Development Manager/Specialist – Creative Economy will support commercial growth within the creative economy by translating Equity Bank’s strategy into financial propositions, partnerships and business opportunities.
The position focuses on creators, artists, athletes, gig workers and digital entrepreneurs and seeks to expand the Bank’s participation in these emerging economic segments.
Applicants should note that the 18 vacancies do not share a single closing date.
Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the relevant closing date rather than waiting until the final day.

Interested candidates should access the official Equity Bank recruitment portal, select the position that matches their professional background and carefully read the complete vacancy notice before beginning an application.
Candidates should ensure that information submitted during the recruitment process is accurate and that all documents requested through the recruitment portal are provided in the required format.

Because each vacancy has its own responsibilities and eligibility requirements, applicants should rely on the requirements stated in the individual official job advertisement rather than assuming that requirements for one Equity Bank position apply to another.
Applications for these vacancies are being handled online through Equity Bank’s recruitment system.

items.title: Kenya Construction Regulator Flags Inspection Gaps After 72 Collapses
items.description: Kenya's National Construction Authority covers only 27 counties with five Nairobi inspectors after 72 building collapses in three years, amid heavy rains.
content: Kenya's National Construction Authority covers only 27 counties with five Nairobi inspectors after 72 building collapses in three years, amid heavy rains.

Kenya's National Construction Authority has warned that severe underfunding leaves it operating in only 27 of the country's 47 counties, even after 72 buildings collapsed nationwide over the past three years.

According to a November 19, 2026 Citizen TV report and a November 20 Kenyans.co.ke update, the regulator faces acute staffing constraints as seasonal heavy rainfall heightens structural risks across active construction zones. In Nairobi, the epicentre of Kenya's high-rise development boom, only five NCA inspection officers are tasked with overseeing thousands of ongoing projects.

The disclosure exposes a central contradiction in Kenya's built environment: while the state replaced a 56-year-old colonial building order in February 2025 with the National Building Code, 2024, front-line capacity to verify whether developers follow those rules has fallen far behind the pace of urban construction.

Leaving 20 Kenyan counties without an NCA operational footprint forces regulators to stretch sparse teams across wide regions or rely on reactive checks after failures occur. With only five inspectors assigned to Nairobi's entire construction pipeline, routine site verification across excavation, foundation curing, concrete mixing, and multi-storey framing becomes physically impossible at scale.

The human stakes of inspection gaps were underscored in Eastleigh, Nairobi, where an 18-storey building collapsed in October 2026. On November 5, the fourteenth day of search and rescue operations, Citizen TV reported that teams recovered six additional bodies, bringing the confirmed death toll to eight while five people remained unaccounted for and families waited for answers.

Increased rainfall across Kenya adds immediate physical stress to compromised structures. Waterlogged soils reduce bearing capacity under shallow or poorly engineered foundations, while unsealed concrete slabs and inadequate drainage accelerate structural degradation on stalled or hurried sites.

Preventing structural failures requires coordination across multiple laws and institutions rather than a single agency acting alone. Under Kenya's statutory framework, responsibility is divided between county governments and national regulators at distinct stages of a project's life cycle.

In practice, that split creates dangerous seams. County governments issue initial development permissions and approve architectural and structural plans under the Physical and Land Use Planning Act. The NCA, established under Act No. 41 of 2011, registers contractors, accredits site supervisors and skilled workers, registers projects, and monitors compliance on active sites.

When county plan-vetting, NCA site registration, and physical inspections fail to align, unauthorised floors, unverified design changes, or unapproved occupancy can persist undetected until a structure fails. Published in Kenya Gazette No.

28 on March 1, 2024 and commenced on February 20, 2025, the National Building Code, 2024 replaced the 1968 Local Government Building Order with updated rules on structural design, fire protection, electrical installations, occupancy certification, and enforcement. Yet updated legal standards cannot inspect concrete pours on their own.

Even when inspectors flag violations, the gap between legal authority and sustained enforcement remains wide across fast-growing neighbourhoods. Developers face intense commercial pressure to finish multi-storey residential blocks quickly and occupy ground floors before upper levels or certification procedures are complete.

Public records reviewed from the November 19 and November 20 briefings do not disclose the exact size of the NCA's current funding shortfall in shillings, nor has the regulator published a county-by-county breakdown identifying where the 72 collapses occurred or how many resulted in criminal convictions.

Under the National Construction Authority Act, contractors, site supervisors, and skilled construction workers must hold accreditation, and ongoing projects must be registered before works proceed. However, without enough county offices or inspectors to verify compliance on the ground, registration risks remaining a paper formality rather than an active safety filter.

For prospective tenants, buyers, and lenders, the practical baseline is clear: verifying both county development approvals and NCA project registration before committing money remains essential, yet self-checks cannot substitute for state inspections. Until Kenya matches its 2024 Building Code with funded inspectors across all 47 counties, heavy rains and rapid high-rise construction will continue to test weak links in the regulatory chain.

content: There is plenty on the line at the top of the SportPesa Premier League standings as we gear up for a potentially explosive round eight this weekend.
Both AFC Leopards and Police FC have the chance to take charge of the SportPesa League with a win in their particular fixtures scheduled for Saturday afternoon.

KCB are currently the SportPesa League leaders with 14 points after seven games, one more than record league winners Gor Mahia in second.
Ingwe are third, level with Gor and Police follow closely with 12 points.
Murang’a climbed into fifth with 11 points after an impressive 2-0 away win against Bandari on Friday afternoon, inspired by SL top scorer Josphat Lopaga.

Homeboyz are now winless in their last seven games and continue to lose momentum in 13th place with seven points.

Leopards enter the match third with 13 points from seven matches, just one point behind leaders KCB. Migori are 11th with seven points from six matches.

Migori have also been difficult to beat. They have won one, drawn four and lost just once, while they remain unbeaten at Green Awendo Stadium with one victory and two draws.

items.title: UK Embassy in Nairobi celebrates King’s birthday by honouring Kenyan sports personalities
items.description: The United Kingdom Embassy in Nairobi celebrated King Charles III birthday party , who turned 78, by honouring Kenyan sportsmen and women on Thursday evening.
content: The United Kingdom Embassy in Nairobi celebrated King Charles III birthday party , who turned 78, by honouring Kenyan sportsmen and women on Thursday evening.
The UK celebrated close diplomatic ties and collaboration in enhancing sports in Kenya and the critical role of Kenya in Commonwealth sports.
British High Commissioner to Kenya Matt Baugh delivered the keynote address and the King’s message, reaffirming their continued support for the growth of Kenya’s sports globally.
Matt also congratulated Kenya on winning the hosting rights for the 22nd World Athletics Championships in 2029, the first African country to stage the global event.

“And as we’ve heard, the largest ever Kenyan team for a Commonwealth Games, 12 medals in all, three Kenyan flags, proclaiming complete dominance of the men’s Steeplechase. In September, another athletics triumph over the Brits, as Nairobi is awarded the 2029 World Athletics Championships, the first on African soil—the first African country to stage the global event,” the ambassador noted.

Foreign Affairs PS Korir Sing’oei, who delivered the Kenyan government’s message, hailed the strong diplomatic ties between Kenya and the UK in various sectors, among them sports, trade, and education. He reassured that Kenya will continue working with the UK to open more opportunities for the benefit of the two nations.

“The Kenya-UK partnership has been carried forward by successive generations, each passing the baton with care to the next. Kenya reaffirms its commitment to running the next leg with ambition, guided by the values of fair play, mutual respect, shared prosperity, and the enduring friendship between our peoples.” stated the PS

Sing’oei also congratulated Team Kenya’s recent performance at the 23rd Commonwealth Games in Scotland, UK, especially the dominant performance in the men’s 3,000m steeplechase where Edmund Serem led the country to a clean podium sweep.

“The Kenya-UK Economic Partnership Agreement has, since 2021, secured duty-free, quota-free access for Kenyan exports to the British market, and in July 2025, the renewal of the strategic partnership by our two leaders in London.”said the PS

The UK also honoured Kenyan sportsmen and women who have excelled on the global stage, such as recently crowned New York City Marathon champion Sheila Chepkirui, former 800m World and Commonwealth champion Mary Moraa, Kenya Lionesses captain Sheila Chajira, and para-athlete Henry Wanyoike, among others.
King Charles III’s 78th birthday was celebrated in the UK on the 14th of this month.

items.title: Manchester United Training Drone Footage: What Pochettino’s First Session Showed
items.description: See what Manchester United Training Drone Footage captured during Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session, the players involved and the Liverpool team news.
content: Manchester United training drone footage captured part of Mauricio Pochettino’s first session with the squad at Carrington on Thursday, 19 November 2026. Around 12 minutes of video appeared online, showing small-group drills and the new head coach working with players. The footage prompted questions about training-ground privacy and how much Liverpool could learn before their Premier League meeting. Here is what the recording, the club’s official team news and the reported accounts establish.

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session took place as the club prepared to visit Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, 22 November, with kick-off scheduled for 19:30 East Africa Time. The Argentine had arrived in Manchester on Wednesday after completing his final assignment with the United States national team. His first on-pitch work was filmed by an independent drone operator and later published on YouTube. United also released its own training update, confirming the involvement of two players whose availability had been in doubt.

The video of Pochettino’s first Man Utd training session shows football exercises rather than a confirmed tactical plan for Liverpool. Sky Sports reported that the 12-minute recording begins with rondos, in which players circulate possession while others attempt to intercept, before showing Pochettino guiding a smaller group through work on an adjoining pitch. The footage was recorded from outside the training complex and published online by a drone operator identified as CC Overview.

BBC Sport identified multiple groups of players involved in the session, including younger footballers and regular first-team names. Their presence confirms participation in that part of training, not a place in Sunday’s starting eleven.

Manchester United team news ahead of Liverpool received a more reliable update from the club itself: Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu trained at Carrington on Thursday. Maguire had been substituted with a back spasm during the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, while Dorgu had not featured in Denmark’s recent international matches. Their participation is encouraging, but match readiness and selection remain decisions for the coaching staff.

The club also stated that Lisandro Martinez was available after suspension. It planned Pochettino’s first pre-match press conference for Friday, when a fuller assessment of the squad could be provided.

Questions about Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United tactics intensified because the footage shows a small group being coached separately from other players. Sky Sports described positional work and a group briefing, but cautioned that those involved should not be assumed to be the starting line-up. Early-session exercises can illustrate a coach’s methods without establishing his match plan.

Pochettino has previously favoured high-intensity work, pressing and collective movement, yet one filmed session cannot show whether those principles will be adopted immediately or how United will line up at Anfield. Any detailed formation claim would need stronger evidence, such as a confirmed team sheet or the manager’s own explanation.

The Carrington filming controversy centres on the publication of training images that the club had not itself released. Reports said the operator maintained that the drone was flown in unrestricted airspace, stayed within visual range and complied with the relevant requirements. Sky Sports also reported that signs near the complex prohibit drones and that Manchester United declined to comment on the incident.

Those accounts establish a dispute about access and privacy, not a legal determination. Nor is there evidence that Liverpool commissioned the recording or that the video changed either team’s preparations.

Liverpool vs Manchester United on 22 November 2026 is scheduled to be Pochettino’s first match as United head coach, only days after his appointment. United enter the trip amid pressure to improve their Premier League performances, while the manager has called for a brave approach to the Anfield encounter. The Manchester United fixtures and results hub covers the club’s wider schedule.

The recording adds another story to a busy opening week for the Argentine, but his early results and team selections will offer better evidence of his approach than isolated training footage. Read our Pochettino Manchester United overview for the appointment and immediate Premier League challenge. For current match scores, fixtures and standings, follow SportPesa Score.

Pochettino’s first Manchester United session became news because 12 minutes of training were recorded from the air and shared publicly. The footage shows on-pitch work and player groupings; it does not confirm Sunday’s line-up or prove that the club’s tactical plans were exposed. With Maguire and Dorgu back in training, attention now turns to the final team news and the Liverpool fixture. The outcome at Anfield will provide the first competitive measure of this new chapter at United.

Media personality Oga Obinna has set Kenyan social media alight once more after posting a breezy car reel that brought DNA testing back into the conversation.
In the clip, shared on Friday, November 20, via his Instagram handles @ogaobinna and @theobinnaz, Obinna is behind the camera inside a moving luxury SUV with an open sunroof.

Seated beside him is a young man dressed in a dark polo shirt and a blue Titleist visor. The two laugh, gesture and chat in a mix of Swahili and English about food, fatherhood and responsibility. Throughout the footage, on-screen text poses the question:
Oga Obinna's former employee Dappa Man gives glimpse of his new studio
PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.
The tone is playful rather than confrontational. No child is named, no test result is shared, and there is no formal announcement of a scheduled paternity test.
The reel reads more like a teaser for an upcoming YouTube episode of the Obinna Show Live than any real-life accusation.
The reason the video has generated so much buzz is that DNA and paternity are topics Obinna has made his own in recent months, both in his personal life and on his platform.
He has previously spoken publicly about demanding a DNA test for his daughter Ada after her mother's lawyer sent him a request for KSh 54,000 in monthly child support.

Obinna said the financial pressure, combined with noticing that Ada appeared significantly lighter-skinned than him, prompted the request. The test eventually confirmed Ada was his, and he later had an open conversation with her about it.
Azziad Nasenya sparks reactions after alleging she has 5 kids: “Watatu wanalala”
The situation with his fifth child, Ella, went differently. When he discovered her existence months after her birth, he publicly declared her his without any test, writing on Instagram:

Beyond his own family matters, Obinna has emerged as one of Kenya's most vocal advocates for mandatory paternity testing. In a video posted in September, he called for DNA tests to be compulsory at birth and argued that women who knowingly mislead men about paternity should be required to repay every expense incurred in raising the child.
No such legislation currently exists in Kenya.

His show has also hosted some of the country's most talked-about DNA storylines, including the Stevo Simple Boy saga, in which a DNA test eventually excluded Stevo as the biological father of his son Dragon Junior.
Onyango Jasuba: Late Ohangla musician's past interview about returning home with diseases surfaces
For now, the latest reel remains exactly what it looks like: Obinna, a sunroof, a laughing passenger and one unanswered question for his followers.
We also highlighted facts about Obinna’s response after his fourth baby mama, Tallie, went public with claims about their relationship and her pregnancy.

Tallie said she secretly had her family planning removed and that Obinna later travelled to her mother’s village after learning she was expecting. His cryptic posts appeared to accuse people close to him of betrayal and failing to tell the full story.

One year after the death of beloved Kenyan gospel singer Betty Bayo, her family gathered at Mugumo for what should have been a straightforward memorial, only to find themselves locked in a tense standoff over access to the late musician's home.
In a TikTok video filmed by MBC TV, Bayo's siblings and other family members spoke, describing a situation that had clearly left them shaken and frustrated.

His brother John Mbugua claimed that the family had made the trip specifically to honour Bayo on her first anniversary. He said they had been attending for her and expected to do so for many years to come.

Betty Bayo's sister, Irene Wanjiku, also appeared in the video and confirmed they had formally invited Bayo's children to the event, sending letters ahead of time.
She added that the family had gone a step further by notifying the local Officer Commanding Station, holding a letter permitting them to proceed.
However, the family alleged that Tash, whose full name is Hiram Gitau and who was Bayo's widower, had effectively blocked them from holding the ceremony at the singer's home.
According to the family, all communication had been routed through lawyers, and his response had done little to resolve matters on the ground.
Another family member, who identified himself as Wendo, described making the journey for the memorial and indicated the gathering was meant to be a modest occasion for family and friends.

None of the family members provided a direct explanation from Tash regarding his reasons, and the matter appears unresolved as of the date of filming.
Betty Bayo was a celebrated Kenyan gospel musician known for her powerful vocals and faith-driven music.
Her passing left a significant void in the local gospel scene, and her first anniversary drew not only family but also public attention given the circumstances surrounding the memorial.

content: Kenya's Cabinet Secretary, Hon. William Kabogo, has been honoured with the prestigious Global Icon in Artificial Intelligence, Public Relations & Digital Economy Leadership Award by the Global Alliance and the Africa Public Relations Association in Abuja, Nigeria.

Kenya's Cabinet Secretary, Hon. William Kabogo, has been honoured with the prestigious Global Icon in Artificial Intelligence, Public Relations & Digital Economy Leadership Award by the Global Alliance and the Africa Public Relations Association in Abuja, Nigeria.

The award recognises his visionary leadership, transformative policy execution, and pioneering contributions to Artificial Intelligence, national connectivity, digital transformation, and the advancement of Kenya's digital economy.

The recognition celebrates Hon. Kabogo's commitment to positioning Kenya at the forefront of the Fourth Industrial Revolution through the promotion of responsible and ethical AI, expanded digital infrastructure, innovation, and an enabling environment for technology-driven enterprise, digital skills, and economic opportunity.
Beyond technology and infrastructure, the award places particular emphasis on his contribution to the evolving role of public relations and public communication in modern governance.

Hon. Kabogo has championed the understanding that government communication must go beyond announcements and information dissemination. It must be a deliberate process of engaging citizens, listening to their concerns, building understanding, strengthening institutional credibility, and ensuring that public policies and programmes are communicated in ways that are accessible, relevant, and meaningful to the people they serve.

His approach underscores the growing importance of strategic public relations in government—not merely as a publicity function, but as an essential pillar of governance, public participation, accountability, trust-building, and national development.

In an era defined by rapid technological change, information disorder, and increasingly discerning citizens, effective public communication has become critical to the success of public policy. Hon. Kabogo's leadership reflects a commitment to modernising government communication through digital platforms, strengthening stakeholder engagement, embracing innovation, and fostering a more responsive and citizen-centred approach to public information.

The recognition also celebrates his efforts to strengthen Kenya's digital ecosystem through expanded broadband connectivity, support for innovation and technology startups, digital inclusion, and international cooperation. These initiatives are helping create opportunities for citizens and businesses while supporting Kenya's ambitions as a competitive digital economy.

The award further acknowledges his role in advancing a progressive national narrative—one that communicates Kenya's ambitions, achievements, opportunities, and place in the global technology landscape with confidence and purpose.

By bringing together Artificial Intelligence, digital economy leadership, and Public Relations, the award recognises a broader vision of modern governance: one in which technological progress is matched by effective communication, innovation by inclusion, and policy ambition by public understanding and trust.

Hon. Kabogo's recognition in Abuja is not only a personal honour but also a moment of pride for Kenya, affirming the country's growing influence in digital transformation, strategic communication, innovation, and technology-driven development.
Distinguished African Leaders Among Award Recipients

The award ceremony also recognised an outstanding group of distinguished African leaders and public figures whose contributions to governance, leadership, public service, communication, and national development have earned them various honours.
Among the other recipients recognised at the ceremony were:
- Her Excellency Dr. Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah, President of the Republic of Namibia.
- Rt. Hon. Alban Sumana Bagbin, Speaker of Parliament, Republic of Ghana.
- Alhaji Idris Mohammed, FNIPR, FAPRA, Honourable Minister of Information and National Orientation, Federal Republic of Nigeria.
- Hon. William Kabogo Gitau, EGH, Cabinet Secretary for Information, Communications and the Digital Economy, Republic of Kenya.
- Hon. Dr. Omphile Marupi, Deputy Minister of Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services
- Hon. Cornelius Mweetwa, former Minister of Information and Media, Republic of Zambia.
- Hon. Felix Kwakye Ofosu, Minister for Government Communications, Republic of Ghana.
- Dr. Shadrick Namalomba, Government Spokesperson and Minister of Information and Communications Technology, Republic of Malawi.

The presence and recognition of such eminent personalities underscored the continental significance of the occasion and celebrated the diverse contributions of African leaders and practitioners to governance, public communication, institutional leadership, and development.

The gathering also highlighted the growing importance of strategic communication, public relations, digital innovation, and leadership in shaping Africa's future and strengthening the continent's voice on the global stage.

items.title: Testing a trading app on your phone? Six tech checks Kenyan users should make first
items.description: Trading apps can open up markets that were once out of reach for ordinary Kenyans, from Nairobi Securities Exchange shares to global stocks
content: Kenya’s fintech scene moves fast. M-Pesa changed how the country pays for things, digital lenders changed how it borrows, and now trading apps are changing how a growing number of Kenyans invest. Downloads have climbed as young users look for ways to grow their money beyond SACCOs and savings accounts.

Most coverage of these apps focuses on returns and strategies. This piece looks at something more basic: the technology itself. A trading app holds your identity documents, your money and often access to your M-Pesa line. That makes its security and performance just as important as its features.

Only install trading apps from the Google Play Store or the Apple App Store. Fraudsters regularly circulate APK files through WhatsApp and Telegram that look exactly like legitimate apps but are built to steal login details and one-time passwords. On the store page, check the developer name, the number of downloads, the date of the last update and whether reviews mention withdrawal problems.

Then check the company behind it. In Kenya, the Capital Markets Authority licenses stockbrokers and online forex brokers and publishes the list on its website. Matching the app’s developer to a licensed firm takes two minutes and filters out most scams.

A trading app needs your camera for KYC, internet access and notifications. It has no good reason to read your SMS inbox, your contacts or your call logs. Some fake investment apps request these permissions to intercept M-Pesa messages or harass contacts. On Android, review permissions under Settings, then Apps, and switch off anything that does not make sense.

At minimum, the app should support two-factor authentication through an authenticator app or SMS, and biometric login with fingerprint or face unlock. Authenticator apps are safer than SMS codes, which can be exposed through SIM swap fraud, a problem Kenyan banks and telcos have warned about for years. If an app only offers a simple password, keep looking.

Many trading apps are designed in Europe or Asia and tested on fast connections. In Kenya, users switch between Safaricom, Airtel and home Wi-Fi, and data bundles matter. Test the app on mobile data before funding it. Watch how quickly prices update, whether charts lag, and how the app behaves when the connection drops in the middle of an order. A good app tells you clearly whether an order went through. A poor one leaves you guessing.
Data use is worth checking too. Live charts and streaming prices can consume a surprising amount of a daily bundle, so look for settings that reduce chart refresh rates or switch to a lighter mode.

M-Pesa deposits are now standard among apps that target Kenya, but integration quality varies. The best apps use official Safaricom payment channels with a recognisable paybill or till number and send clear confirmation messages. Be wary of apps that ask you to send money to a personal number or an agent. Test withdrawals with a small amount before depositing more. How quickly and smoothly money comes back tells you a lot about the platform.

Once the basics are covered, compare features. Useful ones include demo accounts with virtual funds, price alerts, clear charting tools, stop-loss orders, transparent fee breakdowns and in-app support that responds within hours, not days. A wider comparison of trading apps in Kenya , with features set out side by side, can help narrow the list. Use it alongside the CMA register rather than in place of it.

Trading apps can open up markets that were once out of reach for ordinary Kenyans, from Nairobi Securities Exchange shares to global stocks. But the same convenience that makes them attractive makes them a target for fraud. Treat a new trading app the way you would treat a new banking app: verify who built it, lock it down, and test it with small amounts before trusting it with your savings.

items.title: Kenya exploring AI application to improve healthcare delivery
items.description: Kenya exploring AI application to improve healthcare delivery Kenya News Agency
content: The Ministry of Health is stepping-up efforts to integrate Artificial Intelligence into healthcare delivery, while strengthening doctors’ welfare and expanding access to HIV prevention services through strategic partnerships.

Principal Secretary (PS) for Medical Services, Dr Ouma Oluga, held a series of engagements at Afya House in Nairobi with representatives of global health organisations, technology experts and the Kenya Medical Practitioners, Pharmacists and Dentists Union (KMPDU), to explore ways of improving healthcare delivery and strengthening the country’s health system.

In a meeting with Ms. Anne Stake, Global Health Team Lead, at Anthropic BPC, the Ministry explored opportunities to harness artificial intelligence (AI) to improve clinical decision-making, disease surveillance, diagnostic efficiency and overall healthcare delivery.

The discussions come as Kenya accelerates its digital health transformation through the Digital Health Agency (DHA), which is spearheading efforts to strengthen digital infrastructure and equip healthcare workers with technology-driven tools to support more informed clinical decisions.

Oluga emphasised the importance of ensuring that AI applications in healthcare align with Kenya’s national AI in Health Strategy, particularly on data sovereignty, security and responsible technology use.

The engagement also highlighted the potential of AI to strengthen health systems while ensuring that emerging technologies are deployed in ways that protect patient information and support sustainable healthcare delivery.
Stake is in Kenya to engage healthcare workers and county health teams in Machakos and Nairobi as part of efforts to understand opportunities and challenges in applying AI to healthcare.
In a separate meeting, Oluga hosted KMPDU officials led by Secretary General, Dr Davji Atellah, to discuss doctors’ welfare and strengthen cooperation between the Ministry and the union.
The PS reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to constructive dialogue and sustained engagement with medical practitioners, recognising their critical contribution to healthcare service delivery.

The discussions focused on promoting the welfare of doctors and addressing issues affecting healthcare professionals, with both sides underscoring the importance of collaboration in improving the quality of health services.

Oluga also held talks with a delegation from the Elton John AIDS Foundation (EJAF) and Tiko Africa on strengthening sustainable HIV prevention programmes through increased national ownership, predictable financing and strategic partnerships.

He called for expanded access to HIV prevention services, particularly among populations at substantial risk, while urging development partners to align their support with national health priorities and strengthen existing health systems.

The meeting also examined emerging HIV prevention technologies, including long-acting injectable Lenacapavir, with Oluga stressing the need for scientific evidence, affordability, regulatory compliance and adequate health-system preparedness before their wider adoption.
The engagement explored opportunities to strengthen HIV prevention programmes, generate evidence and introduce innovative approaches to service delivery.
The delegation was led by EJAF Chief Executive Officer Anne Aslett and Tiko Africa Co-Chief Executive Officer Serah Malaba, alongside representatives from the two organisations.

The engagements reflect the Ministry’s broader focus on combining digital innovation, improved healthcare workforce welfare and strategic partnerships to build a resilient, accessible and sustainable health system.

items.title: TikTok, ICC Kenya to equip creators with digital commerce skills
items.description: Kenyan digital creators are set to gain digital commerce skills to help them scale up and reach wider number of online consumers.
content: Kenyan digital creators are set to gain digital commerce skills to help them scale up and reach wider number of online consumers.
This follows the launch of the first flagship Digital Commerce Labs (DCL) by TikTok and the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC).
Under the partnership, TikTok and ICC target to train thousands of small businesses across Sub-Saharan Africa in digital commerce skills which will be delivered both online and offline

“Digital commerce is reshaping how businesses grow across Sub-Saharan Africa, and Kenyan entrepreneurs are at the heart of that shift,” said Kushal Prakash, TikTok Head of Global Institution Engagement.
Prakash said social commerce has the power to unlock opportunities, level the playing field and equip Kenyan entrepreneurs with the tools to grow.

“Through our partnership with ICC, we are committed to making sure that the benefits of that transformation reach every small business owner in this region. We have seen how TikTok makes it easier for businesses to be discovered and influence purchase decisions through trends such as #TikTokMadeMeBuyIt,” he added.
Kenya was picked as the first country to kick off the programme given the fact that the country’s cocial commerce is among the fastest growing in the world.
According to GSMA, 49% of Kenyan businesses sell online exclusively through social media, with a further 13% combining social platforms with a website or marketplace.

Head of Presidential Special Projects and Creative Economy Dennis Itumbi challenged the social media giant to avail features such as TikTok Shops to help grow small businesses as part of the programme.

“TikTok Shops is not available in any country in Africa. Kenya is willing to become the pilot market for TikTok Shops. Give us a timeline and tell us what we need to do so that we have TikTok Shops because why then are you training our people if they cannot benefit from those commerce and trade aspects that you already have on your platform,” said Itumbi.
DCL Offer a comprehensive, two-part learning experience designed to help Kenyan businesses harness the full potential of digital commerce.

Participants can access self-taught online modules, developed by local experts and covering topics from building a digital presence and creating effective content, to leveraging AI-driven e-commerce tools and preparing for both domestic and international growth.
The programme will further help Kenyan entrepreneurs and businesses explore real-world digital commerce growth opportunities.

items.title: Edna Karijo Wins Women In Tech Leadership Award At Africa Tech Festival 2026
items.description: Kenya’s Edna Karijo has won the Women in Tech Leadership Award at the Africa Tech Festival Awards 2026
content: Edna Karijo, Associate Director at eMobilis Technology Training Institute, has won the Women in Tech Leadership Award at the Africa Tech Festival Awards 2026. The winners were announced at a gala evening in Cape Town on 18 November, during the 2026 edition of Africa Tech Festival.

The award recognises women who have shown innovation, excellence and leadership in technology across the continent. Edna was shortlisted alongside Majda Lahlou Kassi of Ericsson and Shireen Powell of Project Isizwe.

Karijo leads digital skilling and inclusion work at eMobilis where she has led transformative programmes including Google’s Digital Skills for Africa, Ajira Digital Program and the Norwegian Refugee Council’s area-based livelihoods digital skills initiative. She is also a co-author of She Leads , a book of lessons from women leaders. She was also among the 2025 CIO Africa’s Top 45 Most Influential Women In Digital Transformation.

“This recognition represents far more than a personal achievement,” said Edna Karijo. “It has been a journey of dedicating many years to advocating for access to digital skills, digital inclusion, empowering communities, and creating opportunities for youth, young women, and underserved populations to benefit from technology. All this was made possible through the work at eMobilis Mobile Technology Institute and Internet Society Kenya.”

Edna also congratulated the other winners and thanked the Africa Tech Festival organisers and judges, as well as her family, colleagues, partners and networks. “This recognition belongs to all of us,” she said.

David Monaghan, Vice-President of Africa Tech Festival, said the quality of this year’s entries reflects the depth of Africa’s technology ecosystem, from multinationals to start-ups building impactful platforms.

Kenya Discharges Final Ebola Patient
items.description: 42-day countdown begins as country targets December 23 to end outbreak.
content: 42-day countdown begins as country targets December 23 to end outbreak.
K enya has reached a significant milestone in its fight against Ebola after discharging its final patient, bringing the country closer to ending an outbreak that raised concerns across East Africa.

The patient was released from hospital on November 11, 2026, after recovering from the disease. The announcement marked the beginning of a crucial 42-day monitoring period, during which health authorities must record no new infections before Kenya can officially be declared free of the outbreak.

According to the country's Ministry of Health and the World Health Organization (WHO), the countdown began on November 12, with December 23 identified as the anticipated date for the declaration, provided no additional cases emerge.
The development comes just 37 days after Kenya confirmed its first case of Bundibugyo virus disease, a rare form of Ebola, on October 6.
For the country, the discharge represents an important achievement in containing the outbreak. However, health officials have stressed that the situation still requires careful monitoring.
Kenya recorded nine confirmed Ebola cases during the outbreak, with seven patients recovering and two losing their lives.
The final patient was the seventh person to recover. Before the last discharge, five patients had been released on November 3, followed by another on November 6.
The outbreak began with an imported case involving a Kenyan national who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) through Uganda before returning home.
Subsequent infections were linked to the initial patient and included four family members and four healthcare workers who had treated him before Ebola was suspected.
The infections highlighted the risks faced by frontline medical personnel, particularly when a highly infectious disease has not yet been identified.
However, authorities managed to contain the transmission chain before it spread into the wider community.
A major part of Kenya's response involved identifying and monitoring everyone who may have come into contact with an infected person.
According to the Ministry of Health, all 135 contacts associated with the initial case were successfully traced and monitored, both within Kenya and abroad.
Individuals considered at risk were placed under quarantine and monitored daily for symptoms.

Importantly, health authorities reported that all eight subsequent cases were already under quarantine when they developed the disease. This helped prevent further transmission within the wider community.
The final confirmed case was recorded on October 19, and no additional infections have been reported since.
The last 11 people who remained under monitoring were also released on November 11 after completing their 21-day observation period in good health.
Kenya's response involved national and county health authorities, hospitals, laboratory teams, contact tracers and international partners, including WHO.
The 42-day period is an important part of the international procedure for determining when an Ebola outbreak can officially be declared over.
Ebola has an incubation period of up to 21 days, meaning symptoms can develop anywhere within that period after exposure to the virus.
The 42-day countdown represents twice the maximum incubation period.
This provides health authorities with an additional monitoring window to identify any infections that may have gone undetected.
During this period, surveillance teams must remain alert to suspected cases, investigate potential exposures and monitor the health situation across the country.
If no new confirmed cases are recorded by the end of the period, Kenya is expected to receive an official Ebola-free declaration on December 23.
As of November 20, the country is nine days into the countdown.
Despite the latest development, Kenyan authorities have made it clear that the response will not end with the discharge of the final patient.
The Ministry of Health plans to maintain heightened surveillance and preparedness throughout the countdown period.
Continued surveillance: Health facilities and communities will remain alert for individuals displaying symptoms associated with Ebola.
Rapid response teams: Emergency teams will remain available across counties to investigate suspected infections.
Screening at entry points: Monitoring at airports and other points of entry will continue as part of wider disease-prevention measures.
Survivor support: Recovered patients will receive continued medical follow-up and support as they return to their communities.
Public awareness: Authorities are encouraging people to seek medical attention promptly if they develop symptoms, particularly after travelling to areas affected by Ebola.

Kenya's Health Cabinet Secretary, Aden Duale, also reaffirmed that the country remains open for business, tourism, trade and travel, with no domestic restrictions on movement or public gatherings announced as part of the response.
While Kenya moves towards ending its outbreak, the broader Ebola situation in the region remains serious.
The Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to face a much larger outbreak of Bundibugyo virus disease, with more than 11,000 confirmed infections reported by Congolese authorities by November 11.
The outbreak has also highlighted the importance of regional cooperation, particularly as people regularly travel across borders for work, trade and family visits.

Kenya's experience demonstrates how quickly an imported infection can lead to additional cases, but also how effective contact tracing, isolation, laboratory testing and coordinated public health action can help prevent wider transmission.

For now, the country has reached an encouraging stage in its response. Seven people have recovered, all identified contacts have completed monitoring, and no new confirmed cases have been reported since October 19.
The next 42 days will determine whether this progress can be translated into an official end to Kenya's Ebola outbreak.
